summary:
NASA SPHEREx Sky Explorer is a responsive web application for exploring infrared sky data by position. Users can enter RA and Dec, choose a field of view, and select from five challenge-target shortcuts. The app connects to NASA/IPAC IRSA for official observations and offers a 102-channel SPHEREx HiPS viewer with wavelength labels, six detector-array selections, side-by-side channel comparison, and PNG downloads. Its observation workflow includes chronological playback and image-change tools when date-specific data is available.

The project addresses the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge by helping people inspect how the same sky region changes across observations. Its visual comparisons can help surface possible changes for further investigation; the app does not claim discoveries or confirmed detections. This matters because making large public astronomy datasets easier to explore can help more people participate in scientific discovery. During testing, IRSA’s observation search returned HTTP 502 errors, so real time-separated observations could not be verified. The app reports that limitation instead of substituting fabricated results.
details:
Project Name: SPHEREx Sky Explorer

SPHEREx Sky Explorer is a web-based astronomy application designed to help users explore the universe using NASA SPHEREx infrared observations.

The application provides a user-friendly interface for searching astronomical observations using celestial coordinates such as Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec).

Our goal is to make astronomical data easier to access, understand and explore through an interactive website.

Key Features:

- Interactive astronomy dashboard.

- Celestial coordinate search.

- SPHEREx observation exploration.

- Display of relevant astronomical information.

- User-friendly space-themed interface.

Technology: React, JavaScript, Vite and Node.js.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

The application helps students, researchers and astronomy enthusiasts explore astronomical information through a simple and accessible interface. It aims to make space science more interactive and easier to understand.

Technology Used:

- Frontend: React.js and JavaScript

- Development tool: Visual Studio Code

- Build tool: Vite

- Backend: Node.js and Express.js

Creativity and Innovation:

The project combines a modern space-themed interface with celestial coordinate-based search to provide a simple way to explore SPHEREx observations.

Team Contribution:

Our team focuses on developing the user interface, implementing search functionality, connecting astronomical data sources and testing the application.
